MHS, AIP and OpenMHP serve different reference roles

MHS

Anthropic / HHMI Janelia
Research preview
Shared drivers, capability descriptions and multiple interfaces. Public materials describe institutional trials and vendor plans.

Ecosystem reference

AIP

Supplied PRD v1.1
Design reference
Typed quantities, persistent execution, state provenance and separate control/data paths.

Execution design reference

OpenMHP

Independent community project
Public specification and code
Descriptors, operations, jobs, leases and results. Current device packages are primarily twin-tested.

OpenMHP

MHS warrants close attention. Technical value still depends on coverage, implementation, adoption and experimental results.

AI4Instruments · IOP12 / 16

Basic Operations · Standard Operations · Workflow Operations

Operations compose from basic capabilities into experimental workflows

Operation roleMeaningOptical example
Basic OperationsAn explicit control or observationSet stage angle; read optical power
Standard OperationsA reusable method with stated applicabilityRun a polarization scan and return acquisition and calibration records
Workflow OperationsOrganize methods, instruments and decisionsChange conditions, repeat measurements and select the next parameters
UnderstandExecuteExperiment

Every operation needs meaning, execution and results. Reading levels and operation roles describe different dimensions.

01

The same entry point can lead to very different systems

An MCP service may read one register or submit work to an experiment runtime. Identify who owns connections, state and execution before comparing entry points.

modbus-mcpinstrMCPOsprey
02

Portability comes from shared meaning and procedures

Shared names are a start. Reusable procedures need consistent units, provenance, completion semantics, device differences and result formats.

OpenMHPmicroscope-agentLager
03

Experimental intelligence needs usable experiment objects

Calibration and synthesis agents depend on experiment libraries, drivers and interpretable results. Reusable experiment objects underpin improvements in decision-making.

LeeQk-agentsSynAgent · thin-film synthesis
04

Assess research contributions and released artifacts separately

A paper can establish an experimental method while its public package contains a planner, data or website. Reuse decisions should resolve to files and external dependencies.

ORGANANV autonomous experimentsChemCrow public release

Device bridges

How does an agent call an existing device interface?

What it produces

Callable tools, argument mappings and returned results.

Contribution and value

Brings programmable instruments into agent workflows, contributing integration efficiency and correct result representation.

What to compare

Compare tested models, transports, operation coverage and waveform/image interpretation across bridges.

How to establish it works

Compare tool results with direct-driver readings on a named model and firmware.

Related projects

View all 26
LabMCP · K-DensePackages multiple instrument connectors for consistent installation and discovery.LabLinkBrings several existing laboratory transports into one service.scpi-mcpPackages acquisition goals as scope tools instead of asking an agent to assemble low-level commands.oscilloscope-mcpCombines scope configuration, triggering and waveforms into agent-readable feedback.lecroy-mcpProvides a concrete connection and waveform-acquisition path for LeCroy scopes.siglent-scpi-mcpCovers scopes and supplies while recording the actual instrument commands.
Instrument contracts

Can different devices share capability and state meanings?

What it produces

Device descriptions, quantities, actions, jobs and resources.

Contribution and value

Defines shared interchangeable capabilities so procedures depend less on a particular model.

What to compare

Compare semantics, lifecycles and extension rules, tracking specifications, implementations and physical adoption separately.

How to establish it works

Have two independent drivers implement one profile and run one procedure while preserving observable differences.

Related projects

View all 7
OpenMHPExtends a tool call into a device job with identity, resource ownership, events and results.Open-MHS · Abenor LabsUses capability tags and base classes to make sensing, actions and state discoverable.Open MHS · tongriyaotxtAdds robot actions and skills above registration and command interfaces.Open MHS · SCUT-ESAConnects a common interface to explicit backends and reports tests on two named models.Model Hardware Protocol · CuntinumOrganizes device access around discovery, read, write, execute and shared state.Open Agent Hardware LayerSeparates nodes, adapters, transport and reservation lifecycle, with local and optional remote discovery.
Persistent execution

Who owns connections, resources and long-running experiment state?

What it produces

Device sessions, jobs, events, results and workspaces.

Contribution and value

Separates experiment lifetime from conversation lifetime, supporting interpretable state across users, agents and frontends.

What to compare

Compare connection ownership, recovery, reservations and deployment; a running process alone does not make jobs durable.

How to establish it works

Disconnect and reconnect a client, then recover the same experiment, completed data and current device state.

Related projects

View all 10
instrMCPReuses an already initialized kernel, instrument connections and measurement state.PUDASeparates communication, drivers, procedures and records in a headless execution platform.OspreyLets agents find and operate facility channels through semantic context and facility knowledge.JumpstarterMakes shared hardware a leasable programmable test resource for humans, CI and agents.LagerAbstracts instrument channels as named test points and executes scripts on the bench host.Experiment Automation AgentsCombines image results, workflows and experiment sessions in one agent environment.
Procedure composition

How do devices, steps and samples form reusable experiments?

What it produces

Experiment plans, dependencies, resource movement and procedure results.

Contribution and value

Turns successful operations into editable, inspectable and transferable procedures.

What to compare

Compare procedure representations, concurrency/resources, device replacement cost and execution of generated programs.

How to establish it works

Replace one adapter, reuse the procedure and check timing, samples and result definitions.

Related projects

View all 8
Uni-Lab-OSModels actions, resources and laboratory topology together for multi-device workflows.IvoryOSExtracts operations from existing Python objects, lowering the cost of turning scripts into composable experiments.Agent-LensCombines microscopy, sample handling, analysis services and image data in one working platform.soft-matter-agentsCombines microscope control, simulation and literature modules for soft-matter workflows.OpenLabAIConnects several liquid-handling platforms to natural-language workflows.LabscriptAI OTIntegrates protocol writing, simulation and run assistance in an agent development workflow.
Experimental decisions

How do physical results change the next experiment?

What it produces

Next conditions, experiment choices, updated hypotheses and interpretations.

Contribution and value

Turns tool execution into feedback on a scientific question; value depends on the task and improvement over a baseline.

What to compare

Compare tasks, feedback, baselines and release scope, aligning physical results with what is publicly available.

How to establish it works

Under the same apparatus, budget and task, compare success, experiment count and result quality with full trajectories.

Related projects

View all 13
AILAApplies task decomposition, tool execution and feedback assessment to AFM experiments with evaluation material.LLM-directed-SPMCombines scanning-probe knowledge, command generation and specialized small models for instrument operation.VISIONTranslates natural-language intent into operations executable in an existing beamline environment.k-agentsBuilds a calibration loop of selection, execution and visual inspection around an existing experiment library.Quantum Calibration Agent BlueprintProvides a reference calibration-agent structure for experiment discovery, execution, image analysis and results.CALMSCombines facility-context retrieval with executable functions to connect conversation to operations.
Instrument development

How can agents modify software or firmware and check it on hardware?

What it produces

Program versions, debug state, bus traces and fault localization.

Contribution and value

Connects development to physical feedback so instruments themselves can be improved.

What to compare

Distinguish control-program editing, chip debugging and signal observation from runtime experiment operation.

How to establish it works

Link a code change to a firmware version, physical signal change and reproduction record.

Related projects

View all 4
LabVIEW MCP · ZühlkeBrings LabVIEW programs into an agent’s read-edit-run loop.Embedded Debugger MCPConnects firmware to real chip state so an agent can inspect breakpoints, memory and faults.Saleae Logic 2 MCPReturns real bus captures, protocol decoding and timing results to development agents.MicroPython MCP BridgeUses programmable firmware for board-level I/O and retains hardware descriptions.
GUI operation

How can existing instrument software be used without a suitable API?

What it produces

Screen observations, actions, UI state and output files.

Contribution and value

Extends access to software limited to a graphical control surface.

What to compare

Compare post-action verification, UI changes and data access with any available SDK path.

How to establish it works

Replay tasks on a named software version and assess effects through device readback or result files.

Related projects

View all 1
device-useBrings instrument software without usable APIs into an observe-and-operate loop.
Knowledge and artifacts

How can operating experience and experiment trajectories be reused?

What it produces

Skills, cases, tutorials, analysis code and procedural knowledge.

Contribution and value

Reduces the effort needed to understand devices and procedures and retains operational context.

What to compare

Compare referenced tools/versions, inputs, outputs and experimental conditions; the material does not own device connections.

How to establish it works

Have another user follow the material with the same tools and obtain comparable results.

Related projects

View all 4

OpenMHP

Public maintainer · kushalsinha

GitHub ↗

A device contract covering descriptors, reads, writes, actions, jobs, leases and run records, with bridges to existing drivers. Useful for studying a compact device interface and on-demand discovery.

Access path described in the public material
  1. 01Agent
  2. 02MCP / CLI / SDK
  3. 03OpenMHP jobs & leases
  4. 04device adapter

Contribution and value

Extends a tool call into a device job with identity, resource ownership, events and results.

Distinctions and conditions

Compared with a device-specific MCP bridge, the emphasis is a shared lifecycle and on-demand capabilities; current device-package evidence is primarily twin testing.

Reusable ideas

Reuse job, lease and result structures; establish physical readback and run records for each model.

Public scope and experiment record

Published specification and implementation. Seven supported-device packages are marked twin tested, plus one manual-operation template; maintainers explicitly distinguish these from hardware-tested drivers.

Release type: ImplementationLicense: Apache-2.0Reviewed: 2026-10-20

Interfaces and dependencies

MCP · CLI · Python SDK · JSON-RPC · HTTP/SSE

Device drivers, capability descriptions and agent access

Model Hardware Standard (MHS)

Anthropic research preview; the website retains an application entry point and the announcement describes open sourcing as forthcoming.

Public material describes common drivers, read/write primitives, discovery and physical-description tags, accessible through MCP, CLI and APIs. Exact compatibility requires the released specification and implementation.

Agent–Instrument Protocol (AIP)

AIP PRD v1.1, dated 2026-10-18, supplied for this project; a corresponding public implementation has not been verified.

The design includes a persistent Rust service, typed quantities, actions and long activities, class profiles, state provenance, resource conflicts and event recovery, separating gRPC control from Arrow Flight data. MCP is not a product component in the PRD.

User-supplied AIP PRD v1.1 (2026-10-18); design reference, not a public software release.

08 / 09 · AI4INSTRUMENTS

From understanding the field to designing interfaces

Develop shared semantics, execution ownership, data, procedures and ecosystem collaboration around reusable experimental capabilities.

These design recommendations are derived from the reviewed projects and resolve to capabilities, execution and experimental evidence.

Device capabilities

What should be shared first?

Design choice

Define capabilities, quantities, actions and observations, then small device-class profiles.

Reasoning

Shared interfaces need to express actual observability and model differences.

Evidence of completion

Two models run the same measurement procedure while additional features remain discoverable.

OpenMHPmicroscope-agentModel Hardware Protocol · Cuntinum
Execution ownership

Who keeps ownership of the device?

Design choice

Let the experiment runtime own connections, jobs and results, accessed through stable IDs.

Reasoning

Conversations, network sessions and experiments have different lifetimes.

Evidence of completion

Recover the same job and collected data after client disconnection.

instrMCPPUDAJumpstarter
Data and observations

How should results be returned?

Design choice

Return small results with units, time, provenance and configuration; reference large images/waveforms with integrity information.

Reasoning

Results must support subsequent decisions and independent inspection.

Evidence of completion

Trace an analysis result to its acquisition and device configuration.

microscope-agentsiglent-scpi-mcpAgent-Lens
Experimental procedures

What should become reusable capability?

Design choice

Capture successful scans, focus and calibration procedures as readable programs with parameters, conditions and result definitions.

Reasoning

Reusing a command and reusing an experimental procedure deliver different value.

Evidence of completion

Changing the agent entry point preserves procedure records and structure.

IvoryOSLeeQCLAIRify
Access surfaces

Which agent protocol should be required?

Design choice

Expose MCP, CLI and program APIs above one capability service, keeping models/frontends replaceable.

Reasoning

Existing projects use different access surfaces; an entry point does not replace device meaning.

Evidence of completion

All surfaces preserve argument, job-identity and result meanings for the same action.

PUDALagerOpenMHP
Adapters and maintenance

How can the ecosystem keep expanding?

Design choice

Version drivers, profiles, operating knowledge and hardware records separately and connect them through contribution templates.

Reasoning

Models, firmware, runtimes and experimental procedures evolve at different rates.

Evidence of completion

An external team adds a model through the template without editing the core service.

LabMCP · K-DenseDAQiFi Coredevice-skills
Interoperability

How is a useful specification demonstrated?

Design choice

Validate semantics through shared experiments across implementations/models, retaining distinct simulation, hardware and long-run records.

Reasoning

A demonstration establishes one path; an ecosystem needs agreement among independent implementations.

Evidence of completion

Independent laboratories reproduce tasks, interpret partial completion and contribute compatibility records.

Open MHS · SCUT-ESAscope-mcpplr-mcp
Research feedback

How can interfaces improve instruments?

Design choice

Retain unknown states, failures and manual interventions to reveal missing sensing, readback and programmable capabilities.

Reasoning

Obstacles in real research can guide instrument design.

Evidence of completion

An instrument revision removes a reproducible obstacle under the same experimental task.

Embedded Debugger MCPSaleae Logic 2 MCPAILA

01 · What to build

The useful common foundation lets different agents discover devices, understand capabilities, submit experiments, observe physical outcomes and use that experience in subsequent decisions. Its value is transferable experimental capability: what survives a change of model, instrument or laboratory, and what must be established again?

Existing projects demonstrate several integration routes: MCP wrappers over drivers, CLIs controlling local runtimes, plans submitted to established control systems, GUI operation of instrument software, and robots manipulating laboratory apparatus. These routes can coexist. Describing capabilities already available in a laboratory is often more useful than rebuilding its device access.

The central design problem is connecting requests to physical facts. A server receiving a command, a device accepting a setting, execution ending and an experimental objective being achieved are distinct events. Successful transport establishes only part of that chain.

02 · Responsibilities along the integration path

LayerResponsibilityExisting material
Research and reasoningObjectives, experiment selection, interpretation and program generation.Coscientist, AILA, SynAgent, quantum calibration agents.
Agent accessDiscovery, invocation, knowledge access and result delivery.MCP, CLI, Python APIs, Skills.
Instrument contractCapabilities, units, modes, state, physical outcomes, jobs and resources.SiLA 2, LADS, WoT, OpenMHP, AIP / LAP designs and public MHS material.
Execution and orchestrationConnection ownership, long experiments, coordination and records.QCoDeS/Jupyter, Bluesky, Osprey, PUDA, Uni-Lab-OS, IvoryOS.
Device accessActual calls and model/firmware differences.SCPI/VISA, EPICS, TANGO, ROS, vendor SDKs, serial, GUI.
Physical apparatusMotion, excitation, acquisition, triggers and physical feedback.Instruments, controllers, sensors, samples and connections.

Organize knowledge, control and data separately. Manuals and skills explain operation; the control interface submits work and reports state; large waveforms, images and datasets travel through files or data services, entering agent context through references and summaries. Sampling, throughput and deployment determine the data channel; Arrow Flight is not required for every instrument.

Hard real-time triggers, servos and acquisition timing belong in instruments, FPGAs or local control programs. Agents select objectives and procedures, checking feedback at meaningful points. The MHS announcement’s example of turning exploratory laser alignment into a deterministic program illustrates this division.

NameWhat the available material establishesUseful contribution

MHS announcement · MHS website · OpenMHP specification · LAP paper · MCP Tasks

Acronyms do not establish institutional affiliation. The two MHP projects here are maintained by kushalsinha and Cuntinum. AIP is also used by unrelated identity, communication and workflow projects. Catalogue entries identify authors and full repository addresses.

MCP schemas can represent units, ranges and device-specific fields, and asynchronous tasks already have an extension. Instrument integration needs agreed meanings, device-side implementations and verifiable behavior. Adding fields alone is insufficient, as is changing transport alone.

04 · Where to start reading

Existing environment or questionRead firstContract work that remains
QCoDeS instruments and Jupyter measurementsinstrMCP; QCoDeSFresh versus cached values, durable jobs and shared-resource boundaries.
Portable device descriptions and operationsSiLA 2; LADS; WoT; OpenMHP; the Open-MHS projectsRequired class capabilities, optional features and version compatibility.
Facilities using EPICS / TANGO / DOOCSOsprey; TANGO MCP; EPICS MCP; VISIONChannel semantics, facility context, plan execution and records.
Multi-device experiments and edge executionPUDA; Uni-Lab-OS; IvoryOSTopology, contention, sample movement and job recovery.
Scopes, DAQ, supplies and embedded developmentLabLink; scope-mcp; Siglent MCP; DAQiFi; Embedded DebuggerWaveform scaling, triggers, timing, configuration and firmware.
Microscopy, optomechanics and visual feedbackOpenFlexure-MCP; microscope-agent; Agentic microscope; EAA familyImage/position linkage, exposure, calibration and physical readback.
Liquid handling and chemistry robotsOpentrons MCP; plr-mcp; OpenLabAI; ChemAgentsDeck/sample identity, units, consumables and recovery boundaries.
Quantum and scanning-probe experimentsLeeQ; NVIDIA QCA; Quailbot Pi; AILACalibration state, experiment knowledge, feedback assessment and external drivers.
GUI-only softwaredevice-use; vendor automation interfacesUI versions, post-action verification and data provenance; check for an existing SDK first.

Open licensing, hardware validation and deployability are independent dimensions. A permissively licensed project may have only simulator tests; an experimental paper may release only planning or analysis code. Coscientist’s Commons Clause, LabscriptAI’s commercial-use restriction and Uni-Lab-OS’s framework/driver license split affect reuse. License and experimental-status filters are therefore separate.

Assess ecosystem standing through independent adoption, tested device models, manufacturer-maintained adapters, versioned contracts and interoperability tests. Stars, names and a demonstration cannot substitute for these. MHS’s institutional collaborations are relevant, but the public material does not establish that one instrument protocol has already become a globally unified standard.

05 · A minimal useful contract

These are design recommendations for AI4Instruments. The accompanying JSON is an illustrative draft.

ObjectInformation to retainPractical purpose
Device / capabilityStable identity, model, driver/firmware, capability revision, controllable and observable quantities.Discover what can be done and recognize version changes.
Quantity / observationValue, unit, time, provenance and validity; calibration and uncertainty where relevant.Distinguish setpoints, measurements, caches and derived values; never replace unknown with zero.
OperationArguments, preconditions, expected effects, repeatability and actual readback.Resolve uncertain physical outcomes after communication failures.
Job / activityDurable identity, state, progress, cancellation semantics, termination reason and result references.Track experiments beyond a conversation; distinguish requested cancellation from an actual stop.
ResourceShared physical object, ownership scope, exclusions and conflict handling.Express whether channels can operate concurrently, beyond a single global lock.
Event / recordOrdered sequence, time, causality, run and device identities.Reconstruct events after reconnection, including manual interventions.
Artifact / datasetReference, format, integrity information, axes/units, acquisition configuration and provenance.Keep bulk data outside text responses and trace analysis to raw acquisition.

A device-class profile should require only genuinely interchangeable core capabilities. Optional capabilities and namespaces express everything else. Two supplies that set voltage may differ in ramps, triggers, protection states and readback speed. Generality rests on an explicit shared subset.

AIP’s richer state and activity model is instructive, but its implementation cost belongs in each driver: which states are readable, which are only tracked, and which cannot be determined? A common interface should preserve those differences instead of implying identical observability.

A task identifier in process memory does not establish durability. Specify who owns the connection after process exit, how records persist and how restart reconciles with actual device state. An MCP task, a runtime job and an instrument’s internal program can be mapped, but do not inherently share a lifecycle.

06 · Three concrete experiments

Optical alignment: link observation to action

Basic Operations read optical power, capture camera frames and move mirrors or stages, returning units, positions and timestamps. Standard Operations move within a defined range, wait for settling, sample and fit. Workflow Operations calibrate coordinates, find a peak, track drift, preserve optical-layout revisions and compare runs.

The agent submits an objective and procedure parameters; a local program controls scan timing. Each power measurement must correspond to the actual position at acquisition. If motion produces only an acknowledgement without position confirmation, preserve “accepted, position unconfirmed.” LabMCP’s power-meter component offers an interface reference; its simulated status is not hardware validation.

Long scans: preserve experimental identity across disconnection

The agent submits a plan and receives a job ID from a persistent execution layer that owns connections and data writing. A reconnected interface uses that ID to retrieve events and results. If the scan stops at point 47, retain the first 46 points, the actual completion state of the current point and the termination reason. Partial data is not a complete scan.

Communication timeout, execution failure and an unmet scientific objective need separate meanings. When an action was sent but its response was lost, inspect state and events before choosing another action. Network retry policy must not decide whether to repeat a physical operation.

Liquid handling: samples are resources

Moving from a protocol to robot actions requires explicit liquids, wells, containers, tips, volumes and units. Simulation can check syntax and paths before execution; real liquid properties, aspiration height and residual volume remain experimental conditions.

If a dispense response is lost, another call may add liquid twice. Reconcile through the robot run, events and completed steps. HTTP retries alone cannot make such operations reliable.

07 · Turn the research into reusable engineering

Start with a small experiment with clear physical readback, reuse existing drivers and describe its Basic Operations completely. Package useful procedures as readable, executable Standard Operations, then compose Workflow Operations. Preserve implementations and data so new research can change the procedure instead of relying only on a fixed black box.

StageDeliverableEvidence of completion
Device contractCapabilities, quantities, observations, outcomes and version rules.Two device models share a core profile while optional features accurately preserve differences.
Execution serviceConnection ownership, long jobs, events and dataset references.Actual state remains explainable after session loss, process restart or device rejection.
Procedure reuseReadable plans, replaceable algorithms and configuration/data snapshots.Different agent entry points execute the same procedure while retaining consistent raw records.
Ecosystem collaborationDriver templates, profile registration, contribution rules and compatibility tests.Independent laboratories integrate from documentation and contribute device/firmware-specific reproduction records.

Retain failed, unknown and partially completed trajectories. They reveal missing hardware readbacks, controller changes and procedures worth improving. This connects Instruments4AI integration back to AI4Instruments instrument design and continued development.

08 · Read and maintain the collection

Read the naming and responsibility maps first, then filter by existing equipment. Inspect interfaces, the physical path, experimental status, license and implementation entry points. Compare the missing mappings to the laboratory’s current runtime. There is no need to fork every project: retain upstream links, creating a branch or fork when making an actual contribution.

Project records and protocol/component context live in catalogue.json and context.json. Both HTML files embed those same datasets. sources.json indexes sources; catalogue.schema.json defines the fields; build.py uses the Python standard library to rebuild both languages, catalogues and indexes. Both HTML files integrate the analysis, catalogue, source index, field schema and contract example for standalone reading, offline search and export; primary documents remain accessible through source links.

Review date: 2026-10-20. Sources include public repositories, official documentation, papers and selected implementation paths. Physical-validation status cites author or maintainer records. Components and forks are not counted as independent projects. Future changes should record the specific new evidence and status transitions so the collection remains traceable.

From interface to measurement record

Synthetic data connects capabilities, a request, job acceptance, an observation and acquisition completion. State, physical readings and research objectives are recorded separately.

{
  "schema_version": "illustrative-0.1",
  "example": true,
  "data_origin": "synthetic",
  "device": {
    "id": "example:optical-bench/power-meter-1",
    "class_profile": "example:optical-power-meter/0.1",
    "capability_revision": "1",
    "transport": "existing-driver-adapter",
    "capabilities": {
      "power.read": {"operation_role": "Basic", "unit": "W", "readback": "reported"},
      "wavelength.set": {"operation_role": "Basic", "unit": "nm", "readback": "tracked"},
      "power.acquire": {"operation_role": "Standard", "execution": "local-job", "resource": "measurement-channel"}
    }
  },
  "request": {
    "request_id": "example-request-001",
    "operation": "power.acquire",
    "parameters": {"sample_count": 100, "interval": {"value": 0.01, "unit": "s"}},
    "required_capability_revision": "1"
  },
  "accepted": {"job_id": "example-job-001", "execution_state": "queued", "physical_outcome": "not_yet_observed"},
  "observation": {
    "device_id": "example:optical-bench/power-meter-1",
    "quantity": "optical_power",
    "value": 0.00231,
    "unit": "W",
    "observed_at": "2026-10-20T00:00:01Z",
    "provenance": "reported",
    "validity": "valid",
    "calibration": {"status": "unknown", "reference": null},
    "uncertainty": {"status": "not_provided", "value": null},
    "configuration": {"wavelength": {"value": 532, "unit": "nm", "provenance": "tracked"}},
    "job_id": "example-job-001"
  },
  "completion": {
    "job_id": "example-job-001",
    "execution_state": "completed",
    "termination_reason": "sample_count_reached",
    "samples_recorded": 100,
    "goal_assessment": "not_evaluated",
    "artifacts": [{"id": "example-dataset-001", "format": "application/vnd.apache.arrow.file", "uri": "example://datasets/power-scan-001", "integrity": {"status": "illustration_only"}}]
  }
}
09 / 09 · AI4INSTRUMENTS

Sources and reusable data

Sources, relationships, analysis and field definitions travel with both HTML files for offline search and export. Original papers and documents are linked.

73Projects and research artifacts
70Maintainers and standards actors
323Typed relationships
316Source addresses

The 73 project records and 14 standards/foundation groups are separate. MHS and AIP are in the standards collection. Relationships include 177 documented links and 146 analytical classifications.

Complete research bundle

Includes projects, participants, approaches, the relationship graph, both language texts and a measurement-contract example.

Project facts follow linked sources; route classification, contribution comparisons and design recommendations are editorial analysis. Maintainers follow public repository namespaces, with separate sources for institutional context.

2026-10-21
Scope boundaries and naming distinctions

Harbor

An agent evaluation and environment framework, not a physical-instrument protocol.

Quantum-Harbor

A virtual quantum-experiment benchmark; useful for agent evaluation, not evidence of hardware drivers.

OPC UA for AI Prototype

Its public MCP searches specifications, node definitions and terminology: a knowledge interface.

Agent Interaction Protocol

Another AIP acronym, addressing interaction among agents rather than the Agent–Instrument Protocol discussed here.

Agent Identity Protocol

Another AIP acronym, addressing identity and authorization rather than instrument contracts.

LabMCP · ishaanko

A virtual chemistry lab using WebMCP, distinct from K-Dense’s instrument adapter collection.

SciLink

Analysis, planning and simulation system; a complete reusable physical-device path was not verified in this review, so retained as a research lead.

AuraID · OpenOwlab

The current repository is a literature, workspace and compute-task assistant, not evidence for a similarly named instrument GUI agent.

LabClaw · wu-yc

A skills collection and laboratory operating layer, distinct from labclaw/device-use; names alone do not establish a shared implementation.

GaugeForge/instrMCP

A fork of caidish/instrMCP; the upstream entry is retained to avoid duplicate counting.

LLMicroscopilot

The original poster describes TEM/STM image-simulation backends and links a GitLab repository; it is not counted as physical microscope control.

OPERA

The MIT research release provides optical twins, operator/residual interfaces, frozen records and replay validation. Its README explicitly excludes live instrument control and hardware-specific APIs; it informs feedback design, rather than supplying a public hardware driver.
